::: {.chapter-lead}
This space is separate from the lessons. It will collect exercises linked from the course's control questions. **The structure is being prepared: this version does not define new prompts or solutions.**
:::

## Planned organization

Exercises will be grouped by module, use stable identifiers, and link to the canonical lesson page.

- [Mathematical and computational foundations](#foundations)
- [Text, tokenization, and data](#text)
- [Attention and tensors](#attention)
- [GPT architecture and generation](#gpt)
- [Pretraining and evaluation](#training)
- [Fine-tuning and LoRA/QLoRA](#finetuning)
- [Critical evaluation and advanced topics](#advanced)

## Mathematical and computational foundations {#foundations}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: logits, probabilities, entropy, cross-entropy, likelihood, loss, gradients, derivatives, and numerical stability.

## Text, tokenization, and data {#text}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: token IDs, vocabulary, BPE, windows, padding, truncation, input-target shifts, and dataset leakage.

## Attention and tensors {#attention}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: dimensions, Q/K/V, matrix products, softmax, masks, multi-head attention, RoPE, and information flow across positions.

## GPT architecture and generation {#gpt}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: Transformer blocks, residuals, normalization, MLP, logits, autoregressive decoding, sampling strategies, and KV cache.

## Pretraining and evaluation {#training}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: objectives, training loops, validation, perplexity, loss curves, metrics, comparison protocols, and reproducibility.

## Fine-tuning and LoRA/QLoRA {#finetuning}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: classification, target masking, SFT, overfitting, trainable parameters, LoRA rank, and memory/performance trade-offs.

## Critical evaluation and advanced topics {#advanced}

**Status: planned — prompts not written.** Scope: counterexamples, error analysis, contamination, calibration, RAG, attention variants, and limits of experimental conclusions.

## Linking convention

A lesson question will link to a stable identifier in this section (for example `#foundations`) rather than duplicating the exercise prompt in the lesson. Future exercises should specify prerequisites, difficulty, expected deliverable, success criteria, and references. Hints and solutions will be separated from prompts.
